claims.summary: For births with anticipated poor or life-limiting outcomes, guidance supports antenatal palliative care, a coordinated birth plan with newborn caregivers, and involvement of senior paediatric or neonatal staff when resuscitation is withheld or discontinued [RCUK2025; Garten2022]; no source addresses the size of the attending team.

evidence.quote: When discontinuing, withdrawing or withholding resuscitation, care should be focused on the comfort and dignity of the infant and family and should ideally involve senior paediatric/neonatal staff.
Provision of antenatal palliative care support can be beneficial to parents in the face of certain or uncertain poor outcomes.
the development of a coordinated birth plan between the family, their obstetrician, and newborn caregivers; accessibility when needed to additional neonatal and pediatric specialists

omissions.note: Current evidence suggests that maternal infection is a listed risk factor for needing stabilisation or resuscitation at birth [RCUK2025] and independently predicted PPV or intubation in at-risk deliveries [Aziz2008]; chorioamnionitis also raised the odds of resuscitation in meconium births [Chiruvolu2023].

Logistic regression analysis revealed that among various perinatal factors, primigravida, thick meconium, fetal distress, chorioamnionitis, rupture of membranes ≥ 18 hours, post-term (gestational age ≥ 42 weeks), cesarean section or shoulder dystocia independently significantly increased the odds of a meconium-stained newborn needing resuscitation.

known_limitations.note: Collective authors: PubMed (PMID 42596935) and CrossRef list 'Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine (SMFM)' first, then Sparks TN, Norton ME, then 'SMFM Publications Committee' last. refs.py cannot represent a leading collective (corporate) author, so its first-author MISMATCH for this entry is expected; DOI, PMID, title, journal, volume, issue and pages match. The Reviewer's requested fix (authors 'Sparks TN, Norton ME, et al.' plus a note field) could not be applied: refs.py has no command or option to set an entry's authors or note (build formats authors from PubMed; add-manual takes only key, citation, url, doi, role), and refs.json is never hand-edited. refs.json is therefore unchanged and still lists 'Sparks TN, Norton ME', which also leaves the WARN 'CrossRef lists 4 authors; entry lists 2 without et al.'.

Full text refused (cpr.heart.org HTTP 403; an ahajournals.org fetch was blocked as bot-check circumvention); read as abstract only, so US guidance on risk factors and on who attends births could not be checked. A factor absent from the RCUK 2025 list was not treated as absent from US guidance.
No retrieved source names professions or staff counts, so the attendance lines (c1, c2, c11, c25) and the 2 RN / 2 RT items (c26, c27) are insufficient.
Not applied: RCUK table quotes for c6, c7, c9 and c22 (summaries cite RCUK for an item's absence from its list), some finer locations.
